Are there any time or memory limits that could affect the choice of algorithm for N up to 5 × 10⁵?
Is the input guaranteed to contain exactly N characters on the second line, with no extra whitespace or newline characters?

You may perform the following operation any number of times (possibly zero): - Choose an integer i (1 \leq i \leq N-1) and swap the i-th and (i+1)-th characters of S. Find the minimum number of operations needed so that all 1s are contiguous. Here, all 1s are said to be contiguous if and only if there exist integers l and r (1 \leq l \leq r \leq N) such that the i-th character of S is 1 if and only if l \leq i \leq r, and 0 otherwise.
